S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.

subtypes.Intrusive Memories: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Distressing Dreams: Recurrent distressing dreams in which the content and/or affect of the dream are related to the traumatic event.
subtypes.Dissociative Reactions (Flashbacks): Dissociative reactions (e.g., flashbacks) in which the individual feels or acts as if the traumatic event were recurring.
subtypes.Psychological Distress at Cues: Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Physiological Reactions to Cues: Marked physiological reactions to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.

subtypes.Internal Avoidance: Efforts to avoid distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings about or closely associated with the traumatic event.
subtypes.External Avoidance: Efforts to avoid external reminders (people, places, conversations, activities, objects, situations) that arouse distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings.

S072.name: Negative_Beliefs
S072.description: Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs or expectations about oneself, others, or the world.

subtypes.Negative Self-Beliefs: Distorted beliefs such as 'I am fundamentally bad,' 'I am damaged,' or 'I am worthless'.
subtypes.Negative Beliefs about Others: Distorted beliefs such as 'No one can be trusted' or 'Others are dangerous'.
subtypes.Negative Worldview: Extreme beliefs such as 'The world is completely dangerous' or 'Life is meaningless'.

S074.name: Persistent_Negative_Emotional_State
S074.description: Persistent negative emotional state (e.g., fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame).

subtypes.Persistent Fear: A state of constant fear, anxiety, and tension.
subtypes.Persistent Horror: The shock and terror of the traumatic moment do not fade and remain.
subtypes.Persistent Anger: A state of chronic anger boiling inside or being expressed aggressively.
subtypes.Persistent Guilt: Unceasing feelings of guilt or remorse related to the trauma.
subtypes.Persistent Shame: Continuing to feel shame or humiliation due to the trauma.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.

subtypes.Impulsive Anger: Sudden explosions of anger for trivial reasons or no clear reason.
subtypes.Verbal Aggression: Attacking others with shouting, cursing, or blame without holding back.
subtypes.Physical Aggression: Physically attacking people or throwing/breaking objects.
subtypes.Chronic Irritability: A state where nerves are always sharp and sensitive, ready to explode at the slightest touch.

S078.name: Reckless_Self_Destructive_Behavior
S078.description: Reckless or self-destructive behavior pattern that endangers one's safety or health.

subtypes.Risky Behaviors: Reckless actions disregarding consequences, such as speeding, dangerous sports, or criminal acts.
subtypes.Substance Abuse: Excessive drinking or drug use to harm oneself.
subtypes.Indisicriminate Sexual Behavior: Engaging in unprotected or dangerous sexual activities repetitively.
subtypes.Self-Harm: Actions that intentionally harm or scar one's own body.

symptom.disease_info: Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) is a trauma- and stressor-related disorder that develops following exposure to actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence, either directly, as a witness, via learning of such events affecting close others, or through repeated exposure to aversive details. It is characterized by intrusive re-experiencing of the trauma, avoidance of reminders, negative alterations in cognition and mood, and marked changes in arousal and reactivity persisting for more than one month and causing significant distress or impairment. PTSD can have an acute, delayed, or chronic course, and is distinguished from acute stress disorder by its duration and from other anxiety or mood disorders by the presence of a clear qualifying trauma and trauma-specific re-experiencing phenomena. Comorbid depression, substance use, and high-risk behaviors are common and can complicate both presentation and treatment.

patient.personality: He is a steady, routine-loving retiree who values practicality, community involvement, and quiet pastimes, though he tends to worry and resist major changes.
patient.stressor: Four and a half months ago, Jim underwent what was supposed to be a routine abdominal surgery that was complicated by unexpected bleeding and a brief period of intraoperative instability, leading to an ICU stay where he woke up intubated, disoriented, and intermittently aware of alarms, staff shouting, and his wife crying at his bedside. He later learned that for a time the medical team was unsure if he would survive, and he retained vivid fragments of feeling suffocated, helpless, and unable to communicate while believing he was dying. Once discharged, he tried to return to his orderly routines—gardening, church volunteering, and walks by the river—but nights became increasingly difficult, and he started dreading bedtime, staying up late watching classic movies or pacing the house to avoid the quiet. When his wife noticed how exhausted and irritable he had become, and he admitted he was no longer able to get more than a couple of hours of rest despite his usual habits, they decided to consult a psychiatrist at the suggestion of their primary care physician.
patient.chief_complaint: “Ever since that surgery in the hospital, I just can’t sleep through the night anymore, no matter how tired I am.”

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I lie there for hours, dozing off for maybe an hour or two at a time and then jolting awake with my heart pounding, so by morning I feel like I’ve been through a battle instead of getting any real rest, even though I’ve stopped my afternoon coffee and keep the same bedtime routine I always used to sleep fine with.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
S069.manifestation: Out of nowhere during the day or when I’m drifting off, I’ll suddenly be right back on that operating table or in the ICU, hearing those alarms and my wife crying and feeling the tube in my throat, and my chest tightens so much it feels like I might die all over again.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.
S070.manifestation: I won’t let my wife talk much about the surgery or what happened afterward, and I avoid driving past the hospital or watching any medical shows, because the minute anything reminds me of it I just shut down and change the subject or leave the room.

S072.name: Negative_Beliefs
S072.description: Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs or expectations about oneself, others, or the world.
S072.manifestation: Since all this happened, I keep thinking my body’s a ticking time bomb and that doctors don’t really have things under control, like any little ache or appointment could turn into another disaster and no one will be able to save me.

S074.name: Persistent_Negative_Emotional_State
S074.description: Persistent negative emotional state (e.g., fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame).
S074.manifestation: Most of the time I walk around with this heavy mix of dread and sadness, like a dark cloud sitting on my chest, and even when I’m puttering in the garden or at church I can’t shake the feeling that something bad is just around the corner and that I somehow failed my family by falling apart like that.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.
S077.manifestation: I find myself snapping at my wife over small things—like how loud the TV is or if she reminds me to take my pills—and I hear my voice getting sharp and angry before I can stop it, which isn’t like me and leaves me feeling guilty afterward.

S078.name: Reckless_Self_Destructive_Behavior
S078.description: Reckless or self-destructive behavior pattern that endangers one's safety or health.
S078.manifestation: I’ve started doing things I know aren’t smart for a man my age, like skipping my blood pressure pills some days or walking along the river path alone at dusk without my phone, telling myself I don’t really care what happens, even though I know better.
